title: Introducing Eleven v4 and Eleven v4 Turbo

hook.text: Everything you're about to hear was generated from the prompts shown, with no edits or modifications. Just 11v4.

summary.tone: Cinematic, minimal and confident: a calm off-white canvas with two-tone gradient orbs and point-cloud faces, letting playful, emotional generated performances (film set, news reader, phone call) carry the proof, closing on an understated aspirational line and wordmark.

signature_moments.description: Each voice demo shows the exact prompt (including bracketed audio tags like [voice breaking], [laughs], [checking]) as a two-line karaoke caption under a breathing point-cloud face, with words lighting up in sync with the generated speech.
signature_moments.why_premium: It turns the product claim into visible proof: the viewer reads the input while hearing the output, so the demo doubles as evidence and the restrained typography keeps it elegant rather than technical.

signature_moments.description: Abstract gradient-orb metaphors for each feature: the orb splits into equalizer pill tracks for 'tone', pixelates for 'texture', two outline circles merge via their filled intersection for 'speaker similarity', and a glowing core bursts into a multi-depth dot lattice for '100 languages'.
signature_moments.why_premium: Every feature gets a bespoke, on-brand motion idea timed to the spoken word instead of generic UI or bullet text, with grain, blur and zoom-through transitions keeping the whole piece one continuous camera move.

signature_moments.description: A camera sweep past a giant defocused 'v4' pulls back to a gradient 'V4' in an outline ring, which shrinks into the 'Eleven V4' pill lockup and resolves into the ElevenLabs wordmark with a gradient sweep.
signature_moments.why_premium: The end card is earned through continuous scale/focus changes that echo the badge from the opening disclaimer, bookending the film and landing the brand with a single sync point (impact-labelled SFX x099) rather than a static slate.

hook.evidence: Opens on a bold, verifiable claim that everything heard is unedited generated audio from the prompts shown, immediately followed by 'doesn't just speak, it performs' and a dramatic demo; the first 8 s are text on a plain field, so the visual grab is quieter than the verbal one.

clarity.evidence: One idea per beat: performance/audio tags, professional voice clones with better similarity, long-form consistency, 100 languages, and a low-latency Turbo variant, each followed or preceded by an audible demo. Feature lines are only spoken (apart from 'Intent.' and 'v4 Turbo'), and there is no availability/pricing information.

ui_showcase.evidence: No product UI appears anywhere; the 'product' is shown through prompt captions and abstract visuals, so a UI showcase score does not apply.

motion_polish.evidence: Rotating point-cloud faces, orb morphs (split, pill tracks, pixelate, concentric orbits), intersecting-circle fill, zoom-through bridges, word-synced karaoke captions and a multi-stage logo resolve, all with consistent grain and blur and almost no hard cuts.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchor audio facts plus visuals: 102 SFX candidates over 156 s, mostly music beds plus chimes and reverse swooshes; a reverse-swoosh cluster (x002-x006) rides the orb transformations at 9-12 s, a reverse swoosh (x094) accompanies the giant-glyph sweep and an impact-labelled hit (x099) lands on the wordmark; integrated loudness -11.99 LUFS with a ~132.5 BPM bed. The generated voices are the hero and are left clear; many candidates are 'unsure', so exact SFX design is partly inferred.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Narration is sparse and rhythmic ('doesn't just speak, it performs', 'tone, texture, intent', 'you don't just imitate a voice, you embody it') and the demo scripts are written to show range (crying, accent switch, comic pigeon reveal, clinical call). The feature list near the end is a dense run-on sentence.

brand_consistency.evidence: The same off-white canvas, two-tone gradient orbs, grotesque sans and outlined 'V4' pill badge run from the opening disclaimer to the closing lockup, ending on the ElevenLabs wordmark.

works_muted.evidence: Muted, a viewer sees the prompts and tags typed out and the 'v4 Turbo' and logo cards, but the value (expressive voice output) is audio-only and the narrator's feature claims are not captioned.

overall.evidence: A highly polished, cohesive launch film where demos act as proof and every feature has a bespoke visual metaphor; it is held back from best-in-class as an explainer by the absence of any product surface, no CTA and weak muted comprehension.

localization_friendliness.notes: Long English prompt captions with karaoke timing are baked into the demos (s001, s005, s010; s010 also shows Chinese captions), and the feature story is carried by the voice-over and the generated audio itself; only the abstract visuals and the logo end card transfer without rework.

annotation.typography: Clean geometric/grotesk sans-serif throughout (low-confidence guess: a Inter/Eleven-style grotesk), sentence case, normal tracking. Disclaimer: small regular weight, two centered lines, ending in a tiny outlined pill badge (badge text too small to read). Prompt captions: small regular weight, two centered lines near the bottom; audio tags in square brackets sit in a muted tone while the currently spoken words switch to a darker/accented, slightly heavier state word by word (karaoke highlight). 'Intent.' is a large centered medium-weight word with an accent-coloured full stop.
annotation.what_happens: One continuous 63.7 s segment on a constant off-white background (the detector found no cut, so it contains several visual scenes). 0-8 s: the disclaimer blurs in left-to-right line by line while the VO reads it (w0-w17); a small badge pops after 'Eleven'. ~8.5-10.5 s: the text blurs out as a gradient orb grows, swirls and shrinks to a dot on 'A speech model' (w18-w20). ~11-12 s: the dot morphs into a gradient audio-waveform bar cluster that collapses into three dots, then (12.5 s) explodes into a blurred bokeh particle field with soft colour washes that resolves into two point-cloud faces. ~13-51 s: the two faces slowly rotate and 'breathe' as their dots shift, while the bottom caption shows each generated dialogue prompt (with audio tags) and highlights words in sync with the voices (w27-w110), swapping to the next caption block via a quick blur crossfade. ~51.5 s: the faces fade and a gradient orb grows in the centre on 'But voice carries more than just sound' (w111-w117). ~54.5-55.5 s: the orb splits into small orbs riding inside white rounded pill tracks of varying heights like an equalizer ('tone', w120). ~56-57 s: a pixelated/mosaic square passes over the orb ('texture', w121). 57.5-58.5 s: the word 'Intent.' appears alone, centred (w122). 59-63.7 s: two orbs orbit inside thin concentric guide circles that expand, ending with the orbs scaled up past the frame edges on 'you embody it' (w123-w135) into the next shot.
annotation.build_rebuild: On a flat off-white canvas, render two Three.js point-cloud head meshes with slow sinusoidal y-rotation and per-point jitter, place a two-line centred caption below whose words switch from muted to accent colour on each transcript word timestamp, and between sections morph a canvas gradient orb (radial noise shader) through scale-up, split-into-pill-tracks, pixelate-mask and orbit-on-concentric-circles states.

pattern.description: A gradient orb contracts, then splits into five rounded pill bars that grow and oscillate in height like an audio equalizer before settling into the voice-waveform mark.
pattern.why_premium: One continuous shape morph (orb to waveform) instead of a cut; grainy gradient colours carry across the morph, and bars overshoot and settle with springy staggered heights that read as speech energy.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline: orb scale 1 -> 0.5 (power2.in, 0.15s); swap to 5 pill bars at orb centre with scaleY 0.2 -> random target heights, then animate each bar's scaleY through 2-3 keyframes (elastic.out(1,0.5) or back.out(1.6)), stagger 0.03s from center; animate gradient background-position for colour drift.
build_hint.remotion: Per bar: height = interpolate(spring({frame: frame - i*1, fps, config: {damping: 10, stiffness: 180, mass: 0.6}}), [0,1], [dotSize, targetHeight_i]); orb scale via spring with damping 20 before the split; width fixed, borderRadius = width/2.

events.notes: b02 groups three middle elements (dot and two bars) because no per-bar candidate exists; b01 (union) omitted. Pattern could also be 'other' (shape morph into audio bars); logo_resolve chosen as the mark resembles the product's voice-waveform glyph.

pattern.description: A row of orbs riding in white capsule tracks collapses: capsules shrink away and outer orbs shrink to dots while the centre orb scales up to become the sole focus, then a pixel-mosaic square glitches on over it.
pattern.why_premium: One continuous transform narrows attention from a many-voice equalizer to a single hero orb without a cut, and the pixel texture adds a material, tactile beat timed to the narration's 'tone, texture'.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.track', {scaleY:0, autoAlpha:0, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.inOut', stagger:{each:0.03, from:'center'}}).to('.orb:not(.hero)', {scale:0.1, autoAlpha:0, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.in', stagger:{each:0.04, from:'center'}}, '<').to('.orb.hero', {scale:3.5, duration:0.5, ease:'power3.out'}, '<0.15').fromTo('.mosaic-cell', {autoAlpha:0}, {autoAlpha:1, duration:0.05, ease:'steps(1)', stagger:{each:0.015, from:'random'}}, '>-0.1')
build_hint.remotion: Drive tracks and side orbs with interpolate(frame,[0,12],[1,0],{easing:Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)}) on scale/opacity, staggered 1 frame from centre; hero orb scale via spring({damping:200, stiffness:120}) mapped 1 to 3.5; mosaic cells toggle opacity on random per-cell frame offsets (step, no interpolation).

events.notes: Camera verdict is none; the large scale sum reflects the hero orb growing, not a push-in. Pattern could alternatively be 'other' (orb collapse to hero); spotlight_focus chosen as closest.

pattern.description: The word 'Intent.' splits at the syllable ('Int' / 'ent') as letter colours shift and the full stop shrinks away, then the frame switches to two wobbly gradient blobs that scale up and settle into perfect circles flanking an outline circle inside a contracting outline ring.
pattern.why_premium: The typographic beat literally pulls the word apart to hand off to abstract voice shapes, and the blobs settling from organic wobble into clean circles gives a liquid, tactile resolve instead of a plain cut.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.int', {x:-30, color:'#b0763a', duration:0.25, ease:'power2.in'}).to('.ent', {x:30, color:'#2e6b45', duration:0.25, ease:'power2.in'}, '<').to('.dot', {scale:0, duration:0.2, ease:'power2.in'}, '<').set('.word', {autoAlpha:0}).fromTo('.orb', {scale:0.75, borderRadius:'45% 55% 50% 50%'}, {scale:1, borderRadius:'50%', duration:0.45, ease:'power3.out'}).fromTo('.ring-outer', {scale:1.25}, {scale:1, duration:0.45, ease:'power3.out'}, '<')
build_hint.remotion: Word halves: interpolate(frame,[0,8],[0,30],{easing:Easing.in(Easing.quad)}) on translateX with opposite signs; hard switch on the peak frame; orbs and outer ring driven by spring({damping:200, stiffness:140}) mapping scale 0.75 to 1 (ring 1.25 to 1); blob wobble via an SVG path morph or border-radius interpolation to a circle.

events.notes: Energy peaks mid-burst where the text frame switches to the orb frame (same shot per code), so the handoff may be a hard switch rather than a true morph. No SFX candidates. Camera verdict none; the scale sum is the orbs growing.

pattern.description: Two gradient orbs orbit around a common centre inside concentric outline rings, swapping positions with perspective scaling (the near orb grows, the far one shrinks) while the rings expand, settling side by side on a wider orbit.
pattern.why_premium: A slow, continuous orbit with depth-based scaling turns two voices into a dance (imitate vs embody) without any cut, and the expanding rings give spatial depth and a calm, measured rhythm under the narration.

build_hint.gsap: Put both orbs in a rotating parent: tl.to('.orbit', {rotation:540, duration:3.3, ease:'sine.inOut'}) with counter-rotation on '.orb' to keep gradients upright; drive orb scale from orbit angle (scale = 1 + 0.6*sin(angle)) via onUpdate, opposite phase per orb; tl.fromTo('.ring', {scale:0.6}, {scale:1, duration:3.3, ease:'sine.inOut', stagger:0.08}, 0); radius grows 0.6 to 1 in parallel.
build_hint.remotion: angle = interpolate(frame,[0,100],[0,3*Math.PI],{easing:Easing.inOut(Easing.sin)}); orb x = cx + r*cos(angle + phase), y = cy + r*0.6*sin(angle + phase), scale = 1 + 0.6*sin(angle + phase); ring and orbit radius r interpolated 0.6 to 1 with the same easing; no spring (continuous orbit).

events.notes: Camera verdict none; the scale and pan sums come from the rings expanding and orbs travelling. Energy has a single near-zero sample mid-burst (likely a duplicate frame). Exact number of orbit turns is not measurable from 7 frames.

pattern.description: Hard cut from the wide two-orb orbit layout to a much tighter framing of the same two orbs and centre ring, positions matched left/right, followed by a short drift outward as the orbs keep growing and their gradients shift.
pattern.why_premium: The cut lands on the word 'embody', jumping scale while keeping the composition aligned so the eye stays locked, and the continued post-cut drift hides the cut inside a feeling of forward motion.

build_hint.gsap: At the cut: tl.set('.layout-wide', {autoAlpha:0}).set('.layout-tight', {autoAlpha:1}).fromTo('.orb-left', {xPercent:0, scale:1}, {xPercent:-6, scale:1.05, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.out'}).fromTo('.orb-right', {xPercent:0, scale:1}, {xPercent:6, scale:1.05, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.out'}, '<').fromTo('.ring', {scale:0.96}, {scale:1, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.out'}, '<'); animate gradient background-position on the orbs for the colour drift.
build_hint.remotion: Use <Sequence> boundary for the hard cut; in the tight layout, interpolate(frame,[0,12],[0,1],{easing:Easing.out(Easing.quad)}) drives orb translateX (+/-6%), scale 1 to 1.05 and ring scale 0.96 to 1; gradient shift via interpolated background-position.

events.notes: Code assigns this to shot s002 starting at the energy spike, so the cut itself may be a shot boundary rather than an in-shot event; the measurable motion after it is subtle (low energy). Orb gradient change could be a slowly rotating gradient rather than a deliberate colour shift.

pattern.description: A gradient-filled lens formed by the overlap of two outline circles starts zoomed in and tilted, rotates upright and pulls back while the two circles slide toward each other so the overlap widens into a near-round orb; a soft halo blooms around it at the end.
pattern.why_premium: The geometry itself carries the message: two voices converging until their overlap is almost whole visualises 'better speaker similarity' with no text, and the rotate-plus-pullback reads as one fluid camera-like gesture.

build_hint.gsap: Clip a gradient layer to the intersection of two SVG circles; tl.fromTo('.venn', {rotation:-50, scale:2.2}, {rotation:0, scale:1, duration:0.75, ease:'power2.inOut'}).fromTo('#circleA', {attr:{cx:-60}}, {attr:{cx:-10}, duration:0.75, ease:'power2.inOut'}, '<').fromTo('#circleB', {attr:{cx:60}}, {attr:{cx:10}, duration:0.75, ease:'power2.inOut'}, '<').fromTo('.halo', {autoAlpha:0}, {autoAlpha:1, duration:0.2, ease:'power1.out'}, '>-0.05')
build_hint.remotion: progress = interpolate(frame,[0,22],[0,1],{easing:Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)}); group rotate = -50 + 50*progress deg, scale = 2.2 - 1.2*progress; circle centre offset 60 to 10 px drives the clipPath intersection; halo opacity interpolate over the last 6 frames.

events.notes: Camera verdict none; the rotation and pull-back are on the graphic group. Whether the circles converge or only the group rescales is hard to separate from 7 frames; the lens visibly widens relative to its height, suggesting convergence. Energy rises again at the last frame as the halo appears. No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: A loose sphere of soft red/grey dots continuously drifts and re-densifies as an audio-reactive visual for the voice; the burst is the dots in the upper half shifting and thinning while the narration starts.
pattern.why_premium: An organic, audio-reactive particle form gives the abstract voice a living presence without any UI chrome; soft depth-of-field dots and a restrained palette keep it calm and branded.

build_hint.gsap: Render dots on canvas; per-dot gsap.to({x,y,opacity,scale}) driven by a noise field, duration 0.6-1.2s, ease 'sine.inOut', stagger {each: 0.002, from: 'random'}; modulate radius/opacity with the voice amplitude via gsap.quickTo.
build_hint.remotion: Canvas/Three points; per-dot position = base + noise(seed, frame/fps) * amplitude, where amplitude = interpolate(audio volume from useAudioData/visualizeAudio, [0,1], [2,12]); opacity via interpolate with clamp, no spring.

events.notes: Very short burst (~100 ms) inside a continuously animated particle orb; boxes b01/b02 cover the same moving dots so only b01 is used. Filmstrip frames are crops of the b01 region. Camera move is none; the 0.91 scale sum reflects dot drift, not a camera pull-out.

pattern.description: A stack of nested translucent discs drifts from upper left to centre and settles concentric while an inner sphere fades in and a point of light ignites at its core; wireframe orbit rings tilt around it over a grainy gradient.
pattern.why_premium: Layered translucency, film grain and a single bright focal point make a calm abstract 'voice core' with real depth; the slow settle into perfect concentricity reads as precision and stability, matching 'voice consistency'.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline: gsap.fromTo(outerDisc, {x:-180, y:-90, scale:1.08}, {x:0, y:0, scale:1, duration:0.6, ease:'power3.out'}); then innerSphere fromTo {opacity:0, scale:0.8} -> {opacity:1, scale:1, duration:0.45, ease:'power2.out'} at '-=0.3'; core glow fromTo {opacity:0, scale:0} -> {opacity:1, scale:1, ease:'expo.out'} at '-=0.2'; rings gsap.to rotation continuously (ease 'none'); background gradient position tween ease 'sine.inOut'.
build_hint.remotion: spring({frame, fps, config:{damping:200, stiffness:80, mass:1}}) drives disc translate/scale from offset to 0 (no overshoot); inner sphere opacity/scale via a delayed spring (delay ~6 frames); glow opacity interpolate over 6 frames; rings rotate = interpolate(frame, [0, durationInFrames], [0, 20]) linear; background via animated CSS gradient position.

events.notes: Most moving layers lack candidate boxes, so two manual boxes are used. Camera move is none; the 1.03 scale sum reflects the discs settling, not a camera push. All three SFX candidates look like music bed.

pattern.description: Loosely scattered white dots drift and rotate in 3D until they snap into an ordered lattice, while the camera pushes in and depth of field blurs the near and far dots, over a slowly shifting grainy gradient.
pattern.why_premium: Chaos settling into order is a clear visual metaphor for scale ('infinite duration, 100 languages'); real depth of field, grain and slow camera drift give it a filmic 3D feel rather than flat motion graphics.

build_hint.gsap: Three.js points in a grid; per-point gsap.fromTo(position, {random offset}, {grid position, duration:2.2, ease:'power2.inOut', stagger:{each:0.005, from:'random'}}); parallel gsap.to(camera.position, {z:'-=3', x:'+=0.6', duration:2.5, ease:'sine.inOut'}) plus a slight group rotation; bokeh via depth-based blur/size in the shader; background gradient tween ease 'none'.
build_hint.remotion: @remotion/three: t = interpolate(frame, [0, 75], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight:'clamp'}); point pos = mix(randomPos, gridPos, t); camera z = interpolate(frame, [0, 75], [z0, z0 - 3]); point size/opacity from depth to fake depth of field. No spring; slow eased interpolation.

events.notes: Camera verdict push_in (scale 1.68); it may be a 3D camera inside a rendered scene rather than a 2D zoom. Background uses a full-frame manual box because the single candidate b01 was already used for the dots.

pattern.description: The particle orb disperses while an oversized, out-of-focus gradient 'V' sweeps in from the upper left and racks toward focus, with a second blurred green glyph sliding in from the right edge; the previous subtitle fades out.
pattern.why_premium: Type used at architectural scale with depth-of-field blur and film grain turns a product name into a cinematic object; crossing from particles to letterform links the voice visual to the 'v4' brand mark.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline: orb gsap.to({opacity:0, scale:1.2, duration:0.5, ease:'power2.in'}); subtitle gsap.to({opacity:0, duration:0.25}); V gsap.fromTo({x:-300, y:-200, scale:0.8, filter:'blur(30px)', opacity:0}, {x:0, y:0, scale:1, filter:'blur(6px)', opacity:1, duration:0.7, ease:'power3.out'}) at '-=0.3'; second glyph fromTo({x:200, filter:'blur(30px)'}, {x:0, filter:'blur(14px)', duration:0.5, ease:'power3.out'}) at '-=0.3'.

pattern.description: After a hard cut, the frame slides left from the blurred V onto an oversized '4'; the numeral's left stroke resolves from grey to deep green as it settles, still heavily defocused, so 'v4' is spelled one giant glyph at a time.
pattern.why_premium: Revealing the product name glyph by glyph at a scale bigger than the frame, with motion blur and soft focus, makes the name feel monumental and lets the narration ('The next frontier') land on it.

build_hint.gsap: Container of giant glyphs: gsap.fromTo(track, {x:'+=420'}, {x:0, duration:0.2, ease:'power3.out'}) right after the cut; on the 4 gsap.fromTo(leftStroke gradient stop, {color:'#9a9a9a'}, {color:'#0b3d12', duration:0.25, ease:'power2.out'}) and keep filter:'blur(14px)' constant (rack focus happens later).
build_hint.remotion: translateX = interpolate(spring({frame, fps, config:{damping:200, stiffness:200}}), [0, 1], [420, 0]) on a row of oversized glyphs (no overshoot); gradient colour mixes via interpolateColors(frame, [0, 8], ['#9a9a9a', '#0b3d12']); CSS blur fixed.

events.notes: The first energy spike is a cut into shot s011, so most of the change is the cut plus a short left slide. Candidate b02 is a thin sliver at b01's right edge with no distinct element, so it is not used. Camera move is none; pan_x -0.42 is the glyph track sliding.

pattern.description: A large, blurred V4 wordmark sharpens while a gradient pill outline closes in around it from beyond the frame edges, then the whole lockup shrinks to a small centred badge.
pattern.why_premium: One continuous move turns a full-screen title into a compact product badge: blur-to-sharp focus pull, the outline wrapping the mark, and a decisive scale-down give it a crafted, lens-like feel instead of a cut.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline: gsap.fromTo('.v4-text', {filter:'blur(12px)'}, {filter:'blur(0px)', duration:0.4, ease:'power2.out'}); simultaneously gsap.fromTo('.v4-pill', {scale:3.2}, {scale:1, duration:0.8, ease:'power3.inOut'}); then gsap.to('.v4-lockup', {scale:0.15, duration:0.35, ease:'power4.in'}) as the pill finishes. Pill stroke uses a conic/linear gradient.
build_hint.remotion: Drive pill scale with interpolate(frame, [0, 24], [3.2, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)}) and text blur with interpolate(frame, [0, 12], [12, 0]); then a lockup scale from 1 to 0.15 over frames 24-34 via spring({damping: 200, stiffness: 180}) (no overshoot).

events.notes: camera.move reports pull_out; it reads as the lockup scaling down rather than a true camera move, since the background is flat. Corner boxes b03-b06 are the pill stroke exiting the frame edges, not separate elements.
